messages:
Sara: Heads up — we saw a 3x spike in eu-west GPU pool queueing for ~10m, a bunch of SDK clients churned retries and worsened the tail 429 situation. Noticed client-side retries in logs: many 50-200ms retry loops.
Miguel: ugh, saw that alert. did the pool autoscale?
Sara: autoscale kicked but slow because instances need initialization. by the time capacity arrived the queue was still deep.
Priya: can we emit a stronger signal to clients than a plain 429? Retry bursts are the killer.
Jens: agree. current Retry-After is too coarse for per-shard pressure. thinking of a tiny circuit-breaker header + admit window hint.
Sara: proposal: include header: `X-RW-CB: open;ttl=120` and `X-RW-ADMIT-MS: 250` on 429s when pool-level queue > 500ms tail. clients should treat CB as immediate stop for TTL and not retry.
Kyle: +1. also add `X-RW-PREFERRED-REGION: us-west` when geo fallback is cheap. clients can switch region if available.
Priya: can we standardize semantics: CB open = stop all retries for TTL, ADMIT-MS = suggested per-request spacing, Preferred-region = optional fallback hint.
Miguel: what about partial acceptance? like can we tell clients "you can send at 1 req/second"? ADMIT-MS maps to that. ADMIT-MS=1000 -> 1/s.
Jens: exact. also include a `reason` token so clients report telemetry: `X-RW-CB: open;ttl=120;reason=pool-saturation` so SRE can correlate.
Sara: example 429 response headers we discussed:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 5
X-RW-CB: open;ttl=120;reason=pool-saturation
X-RW-ADMIT-MS: 250
X-RW-PREFERRED-REGION: eu-north
```
Miguel: client behavior suggestion: on 429 with CB open -> stop retries until cb ttl expires; update circuit-breaker metric; switch to fallback region if enabled; if ADMIT-MS present, pace any queued requests at that spacing.
Priya: need to be explicit about jitter + backoff: recommend full jitter + min(base, server-admit) semantics. i.e. pick delay = random(0, min(client_backoff_cap, ADMIT-MS)).
Kyle: also add a short token to header so we can invalidate: `cb-id=abcd1234`. would help tracing.
Jens: on server side we tag the CB per GPU-pool shard. we can publish `X-RW-CB-SHARD: shard-12` for internal clients too. external clients ignore.
Priya: implications for SDK: we need default policies: 1) honor CB header 2) stop immediate retries 3) surface a `circuit_open` event on telemetry 4) allow user config to fallback region.
Sara: agree. these changes should be opt-out via SDK config for now. we don't want to break existing customers unexpectedly.
Miguel: ops note: when we open CB too aggressively we may underutilize capacity. need hysteresis: open when queue_95 > 500ms for 30s, close after 3 consecutive 95th < 200ms.
Jens: also publish a metric `client_backoff_fill_rate` to see how many clients followed hint.
Kyle: cost note: if clients flood fallback regions we'll shift load and might blow out quotas there. need cross-region rate limits in the router.
Priya: add server-side guard: only suggest fallback if fallback_capacity_estimate > 10% and region_quota_ok=true. otherwise omit Preferred-region header.
Sara: quick patch plan: eng-infra will emit headers + cb-id. eng-runtime will surface shard id and reasons. SDK team will add honor-CB + pacing. devex to draft recommended client policy text for public docs.
Jens: timeline?
Sara: patch in infra this week (PRs open), runtime follow-up early next week, SDK PR in 2 weeks. rollouts opt-in for 2 weeks, then enable default after telemetry looks healthy.
Miguel: can deploy-bot post canary metrics to #eng-sre when we roll?
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: infra/cb-hint v1 -> canary 10% eu-west 15:00 UTC. health checks: queue_95, 429_rate, client_cb_adherence.
Kyle: one more: add short example in SDK README for recommended reconnection strategy: code snippet with pacing and cb TTL honor.
Priya: sounds good. I'll add testcases: simulate clients that ignore CB and verify router throttles them harder.
Sara: thanks everyone. follow-ups: I'll open the infra PR and tag SDK/Runtime. :thumbsup:
Miguel: thanks, appreciate the quick sync.
Jens: will pair on the hysteresis thresholds with SRE.
Kyle: i'll draft the README snippet and post a link here later.
Sara: done for now, closing thread.
